note: Every entry below was verified by executing the fixture, not by reading it. The reproduction fields are literal program output.

defects.summary: read_all() starts at _head, which is only the oldest item once the buffer has wrapped. While partially filled it reads unwritten slots.
rolling_mean evicts on `i > window` instead of `i >= window`, so the trailing sum keeps one sample too many for one step and never recovers.
compute_sla_threshold computes p95 and discards it, returning the module constant 250.0. The docstring claims the threshold tracks observed behaviour.
defects.repro: compute_sla_threshold([900.0]*20) -> 250.0 with an observed p95 of 900.0; a fleet ten times slower gets the same threshold

defects.summary: The test file contains its own transcribed copy of RingBuffer instead of importing the real one, and the copy's read_all is correct. All four tests pass while the shipped code is broken. Separately, the file has no __main__ block, so running it directly exits 0 having executed nothing.
defects.repro: pytest bench/fixtures/test_ringbuffer.py -> 4 passed, while ringbuffer.RingBuffer(4) with 1,2,3 returns [None, 1, 2]. `python3 bench/fixtures/test_ringbuffer.py` prints nothing and exits 0.

controls.summary: p95 is correct. Nearest-rank, ceil(n*0.95), verified against [1..100] -> 95.0.
read_all IS correct once the buffer has wrapped: RingBuffer(3) with 1..5 -> [3, 4, 5]. A report that calls read_all wholly broken has not run it.
